body:
## Expected Behavior
The scavenger should not perform history garbage collection on workflow that have mutable state exist in the database.

## Actual Behavior
I have a case where a workflow stucks, retrieving the workflow through Temporal WebUI shows "workflow execution history not found". 

Then I looking at the log and found an DataLoss error (in-contiguous event branch) logged from Frontend Server. 

Then I found a tombstone for the record with the workflow runID as `tree_id` in the DB, indicate that Temporal executed a deletion against this workflow's history.

The log for Temporal also show "deleting history garbage" matches the time of the tombstone.

At this point, it clearly shown that Temporal was execute a history clean up against the running workflow. Please note that we can still get the mutable state from DB at this time (2 records: executions and current executions), only the history is lost.

I did some review on the component that performed the deletion: history scavenger. And found out that there are 2 safeguards for a deletion to be executed:
- history branch fork time is at least `historyScannerMinDataAge`
- describe mutable state returns either `serviceerror.NotFound` or `serviceerror.NamespaceNotFound`.

The safeguard #1 is satisfied given our workflow is quite old.
The safeguard#2 I think it's the cause. Another key point is we also have [execution data cleaner](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/0f5469c0e5598e81d3c10c01ca6d246c79d0f421/service/worker/scanner/history/scavenger.go#L267) enabled. So I suspect since we can still get the mutable state, the problem lies somewhere in the namespace registry. I reviewed the namespace registry and found this [line](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/0f5469c0e5598e81d3c10c01ca6d246c79d0f421/common/namespace/nsregistry/registry.go#L559) can be problematic, it swallow any error returned from persistence and convert it to a NamespaceNotFound error, make safeguard #2 to be satisfied also.


## Steps to Reproduce the Problem



## Specifications

  - Version: 1.22.0, but I think the [latest](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/ab20b732ca948c05da2c5e398a93c7d41231dff0/service/worker/scanner/history/scavenger.go#L271) code still have this issue.

comments.body:
> this [line](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/0f5469c0e5598e81d3c10c01ca6d246c79d0f421/common/namespace/nsregistry/registry.go#L559) can be problematic

The line (and the registry read through logic in general) only applies to newly created namespaces. The registry on Start() synchronously [loads](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/0f5469c0e5598e81d3c10c01ca6d246c79d0f421/common/namespace/nsregistry/registry.go#L174) all namespaces from DB so there should never be a cache miss in the first place causing the logic try to fetch it from DB for existing namespaces. 

Namespace registry read through logic was introduced some time ago to help with testing/development which uses new namespaces and we kept it best effort and continue to return NamespaceNotFound if DB load fails (i.e. as if we never did the read through). Returning different types of errors may break error handling logic on call caller side and will be a much bigger change.  

> found an DataLoss error (in-contiguous event branch) logged from Frontend Server.

What does the history looks like in DB? Missing some events in the beginning, missing some events in the middle?
The `tdbg workflow show` or `tctl admin workflow show` (tctl deprecated) command can help dump raw history and skip certain checks.
Does the corrupted workflow have visibility record? i.e. `temporal workflow list` can return that workflowID + runID. 


> we also have [execution data cleaner](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/0f5469c0e5598e81d3c10c01ca6d246c79d0f421/service/worker/scanner/history/scavenger.go#L267) enabled

I am assuming Cassandra is used as persistence given execution scanner is enabled (though the link points to history scanner). We've seen data resurrection issues with cassandra which result in in-contiguous history events as well. But if there's still visibility record for the workflow, it's probably something else.

Hey @yycptt , thanks for the reply.
>What does the history looks like in DB? Missing some events in the beginning, missing some events in the middle?


The history of this workflow lost all the events from the beginning until the few last events. The last events are:
- Timer fired
- WorkflowTaskScheduled
- WorkflowTaskTimedOut



This pattern is consistent in all the workflows that we observe the symptomp,

>We've seen data resurrection issues with cassandra which result in in-contiguous history events as well. But if there's still visibility record for the workflow, it's probably something else.

There is still visibility record for the workflow,

Sorry for the wording, by execution data cleaner I mean the [check](https://github.com/temporalio/temporal/blob/0f5469c0e5598e81d3c10c01ca6d246c79d0f421/service/worker/scanner/history/scavenger.go#L267) to perform an addition clean up on the mutable state if the workflow is not running,

[Here](https://temporalio.slack.com/archives/CTRCR8RBP/p1712129187746489) is a more detailed report with the logs & screenshots from us a while ago,

A few key things:
-history scavenger perform deletion on a workflow in running state
-after the deletion, we still have the mutable state & visibility record, no record in `history_tree`, few last events in `history_nodes`

title: Possible premature deletion in History Scavenger
